## Projects {.i-folder}

All sessions in Emaki are project-based, all listed in the sidebar. You can pin your selected projects and show or hide sessions. To start a new session, you can either click the [+]{.kbd} button on an existing project or press [⌘T]{.kbd} in the project you are in. With [⌘N]{.kbd}, you can start one anywhere (the same as going to your landing page).

Put away ([⌘⇧B]{.kbd}), the sidebar folds to a rail of icons: search, New Session, All Sessions, Agents, and Projects, which opens your projects beside the rail until you choose one.

## Sessions {.i-scroll}

### In the sidebar

Sessions are managed under their projects. A session's leading logo tells you which agent it belongs to and lights up while the agent runs. A dot shows where the session stands: orange while a question waits for you, blue while the agent works or something it started still runs, green for half an hour after it finishes. A bar at the left marks a session that is open in a tab. Claude Code and Codex sessions sit side by side, each read from the agent's own files.

### All Sessions

All Sessions ([⌘L]{.kbd}) lists every project and session with the day it was last used. This page provides plenty of ways of easily managing your existing sessions.

## Archiving {.i-archive}

Claude Code deletes its transcripts after 30 days. Emaki copies each one into `~/.emaki/archive`. Codex never deletes sessions by age, so Emaki reads them in place.

Archived sessions cannot be interacted. You can actively archive/unarchive your sessions. When you unarchive a Claude Code session, it will be treated as if it were created by the time you unarchive it.

## Tabs {.i-copy}

Each open session is a tab, grouped by project. [⌘1]{.kbd} to [⌘9]{.kbd} switch tabs, [⌘W]{.kbd} closes one, [⌘⇧T]{.kbd} reopens the last one closed, and you can drag tabs to reorder them.
